title: Constant scalar restriction identifies geometric module adjunctions
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be sites small in one coefficient universe and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ be a geometric morphism, with $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ and $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Fix a commutative ring $B$, constant ring sheaves $R_C=\underline B_C$, $R_D=\underline B_D$ and their constant units $\iota_C,\iota_D$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Supply a ring isomorphism $b:u^{-1}R_C\cong R_D$ whose adjunct $\gamma:R_C\to u_*R_D$ takes constant scalar $a$ to constant scalar $a$; this equality is an equality of maps from the constant presheaf. Write $u_R^*\dashv u_{*,R}$ for the ringed module adjunction along $b$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], and $u_B^*\dashv u_{*,B}$ for the induced geometric adjunction on sheaves of fixed-$B$ modules. Let $C_C,C_D$ be the actual constant-scalar restriction functors [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], with their inverse equivalences given by extending local scalar actions. There are natural isomorphisms
$$C_Cu_{*,R}\cong u_{*,B}C_D,\qquad C_Du_R^*\cong u_B^*C_C.$$
The first is the identity on the common underlying additive direct-image sheaf. The second is its adjunction mate: after the displayed comparisons both Hom adjunction bijections, units and counits agree. For an open localization $j$ of these topoi, suppose the ringed and fixed-$B$ open pullbacks have their specified left adjoints $j_{!,R}$ and $j_{!,B}$. There is a natural isomorphism $C_Cj_{!,R}\cong j_{!,B}C_D$ compatible with these adjunctions, including their units and counits. This includes restriction to every localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; no hypothesis on points, coefficients being finite, or an underlying scheme is made.

proof.text: Construct the constant scalar map from the sheafified terminal presheaf. Since the terminal presheaf is already a sheaf, every section is in the image of its sheafification unit. Naturality of sheafification and its forgetful comparison identify the scalar map sectionwise with the constant-ring sheafification unit.

Compose the supplied underlying direct-image comparisons to obtain theta. Apply the ringed module_linear and fixed-scalar linear equations to b*x+y, using the normalization hypothesis to identify the scalar inputs. Adjunction injectivity shows theta preserves this operation on generalized elements. Evaluate on the two projections of the product sheaf to get sectionwise linearity; deduce additivity and preservation of zero. Bundle these linear maps, use reflection of isomorphisms by forgetting module structure, and the supplied naturality equations to obtain beta and its underlying-map equation.

For a square of adjunctions with fully faithful horizontal functors F and G, with G essentially surjective, take the mate delta of beta. Its Hom equation follows from the mate unit equation and naturality. The adjunction bijections, full faithfulness, and beta show precomposition with delta is bijective on targets in the image of G; essential surjectivity extends this to every target. The coyoneda isomorphism criterion makes delta an isomorphism. Invert it to get alpha. The unit and counit mate equations give both displayed compatibility equations.

The constant-ring restriction equivalences supply full faithfulness and essential surjectivity of both horizontal functors. Apply the preceding adjunction-square argument to aR and q.adj with beta. Apply the same argument a second time, with the two sites reversed and right-adjoint comparison alpha, to the supplied further left adjoints. This gives kappa with all three required equations. The construction works for arbitrary small sites, including localized sites; no separate localization construction occurs in this Lean statement.
